coachingPoints: Stay low on the retreat — standing up hands the defender an opening to swipe.
Two to three hard back-dribbles are enough; retreat is an escape, not a new address.
Eyes up the entire time; scan for the open teammate before you start retreating.
Keep the ball on your outside hand, away from the defender chasing you.
Combine the retreat with a change of pace — a quick re-attack after retreating is the real payoff.
commonMistakes: Retreating too far and killing your own attack — fix: 3–5 feet of space is plenty; anything more invites a trap.
Palm carrying the ball on the back-dribble — fix: keep fingers pushing down on top of the ball, even while moving backward.
Looking at the floor while backing up — fix: your eyes are your radar; look up and find the pass or the re-attack lane.
Retreating straight into a corner — fix: know where the sideline is; retreat toward the middle of the floor whenever possible.
description: Back-dribble away from pressure to create space without picking up the ball — the smart escape every guard needs.
gameSituations: Beating a full-court press — a controlled retreat lets the trap come to you, then you pass over it or re-attack.
When a defender crowds your space — retreat 3–4 feet, then drive into the gap he just left.
Late-clock situations — keep your dribble alive, create a few feet of separation, and set up the final shot.

howTo.detail: When a defender gets chest-to-chest, take one or two hard dribbles backward. Push off your front foot and keep your stance low — never hop upright.
howTo.title: Back-dribble with force

howTo.detail: Your body stays between the defender and the ball. Lean slightly into him so your back shields the dribble.
howTo.title: Protect the ball with your body

howTo.detail: Lift your eyes and scan the floor while retreating. Look for the teammate the pressure just opened up, or the lane you will re-attack.
howTo.title: Look up as you retreat

howTo.detail: Once you have 3–5 feet of space, make a decision in one second: pass over the pressure, or attack the new space immediately.
howTo.title: Create space, then decide fast

howTo.detail: One escape step should not become ten. Drill retreating to a cone 5 feet away and immediately driving back past it.
howTo.title: Re-attack after the escape

title: Retreat Dribble
whatIsIt: A retreat dribble is a backward dribble — you back-dribble two to five feet to escape defensive pressure while keeping your dribble alive. Instead of panicking and picking up the ball when a defender crowds you, you calmly create space.

It is one of the first 'smart' moves young players should learn, because it teaches composure. Great ball handlers do not fight pressure head-on; they step back, breathe, and choose their next move with room to operate.
whyItMatters: Most turnovers happen when a pressured player rushes and throws the ball away. The retreat dribble gives you a legal, safe way to buy time and space — and time is exactly what good decisions need. Teams that press hate players who retreat calmly, because every trap depends on the ball handler panicking.
